from solution import closest_num


def test_issue_example_11_returns_10():
    """Example: assert closest_num(11) == 10."""
    # 11 - 1 = 10
    assert closest_num(11) == 10


def test_issue_single_digit_returns_previous():
    """Closest smaller than 5 is 4."""
    # 5 - 1 = 4
    assert closest_num(5) == 4


def test_issue_one_returns_zero():
    """Closest smaller than 1 is 0."""
    # 1 - 1 = 0
    assert closest_num(1) == 0


def test_issue_zero_returns_negative_one():
    """Closest smaller than 0 is -1."""
    # 0 - 1 = -1
    assert closest_num(0) == -1


def test_issue_negative_returns_previous():
    """Closest smaller than -3 is -4."""
    # -3 - 1 = -4
    assert closest_num(-3) == -4


def test_issue_round_hundred_returns_99():
    """Closest smaller than 100 is 99."""
    # 100 - 1 = 99
    assert closest_num(100) == 99


def test_issue_large_million_returns_previous():
    """Closest smaller than 1000000 is 999999."""
    # 1000000 - 1 = 999999
    assert closest_num(1000000) == 999999


def test_contract_result_is_smaller_than_input():
    """Contract: result must be a smaller number than n."""
    # 20 - 1 = 19
    assert closest_num(20) == 19


def test_contract_result_is_closest_below_input():
    """Contract: result must be the closest smaller number than n."""
    # 21 - 1 = 20
    assert closest_num(21) == 20


def test_contract_negative_stays_smaller_than_input():
    """Contract: for negative n result must still be smaller than n."""
    # -100 - 1 = -101
    assert closest_num(-100) == -101
